sections.title: Mise en route (5 min)

sections.title: Coin musique (10 min)
sections.intro: Faites écouter une ou deux chansons de chaque artiste, puis demandez :

items.name: Juliette Gréco
items.description: Juliette Gréco was a renowned French singer and actress, famous for her deep, expressive voice and her significant contributions to the French chanson genre. She became an icon of post-war French culture, known for her poetic and emotive singing style, often collaborating with prominent French poets and songwriters. Her career spanned several decades, during which she also acted in films and theatrical productions.

items.name: Fréhel
items.description: Fréhel, born Marguerite Boulc'h, was a prominent French singer and actress famous for her powerful and emotional performances in the chanson genre during the early 1900s. She was a key figure in Parisian cabaret and musette scenes, known for her distinctive voice and heartfelt delivery. Her career was marked by both critical acclaim and personal struggles, making her an iconic figure in French popular music history.

items.name: Carla Bruni
items.description: Carla Bruni is an Italian-French singer-songwriter and former model who gained fame for her intimate, melodic songs often rooted in the French chanson tradition. She began her career as a model before transitioning to music, releasing several albums that blend folk, pop, and acoustic styles. Bruni is also known for her marriage to former French President Nicolas Sarkozy, which brought her additional public attention beyond her artistic career.

items.name: Françoise Hardy
items.description: Françoise Hardy is a French singer-songwriter and occasional actress whose cool, intimate vocal style and sophisticated image made her one of the defining figures of 1960s French pop and the yé-yé movement. She shot to fame with the 1962 hit "Tous les garçons et les filles," and over decades released albums in French and several other languages, earning a reputation as both a fashionable icon and a thoughtful, melancholic songwriter. Hardy continued recording and touring across many decades, influencing generations of Francophone and international artists with her minimal arrangements, lyrical introspection and elegant persona.

items.name: Yves Montand
items.description: Yves Montand was a French-Italian singer and actor famous for his smooth voice, charismatic stage presence, and contributions to French chanson and cinema. Born Ivo Livi in Italy, he moved to France and became a celebrated figure in French popular culture, known for his romantic and socially conscious songs as well as his film roles.

items.name: Paris Combo
items.description: Paris Combo is a French musical group formed in the mid-1990s, known for their eclectic blend of chanson, jazz, pop, and world music styles. The band combines vintage French chanson with elements of swing, jazz, and electro swing, creating a unique and vibrant sound. Their music often features lively rhythms, accordion, and a mix of male and female vocals, capturing a retro yet contemporary vibe. The group gained international recognition for their sophisticated and playful approach to French popular music.

sections.title: Warm-up (5 min)
questions: When you were young in Porto, what did the streets smell like?
What did you and your friends do on a Sunday in the 1950s?
Who was the best cook in your family? What did they make?

sections.title: Music corner (10 min)
sections.intro: Play one or two songs from each artist, then pause and ask:

items.name: Mariza
items.description: Mariza is a renowned Portuguese fado singer who has played a significant role in popularizing and modernizing fado music internationally. Born Mariza Rodrigues Pereira in Mozambique and raised in Lisbon, Portugal, she blends traditional fado with contemporary influences, bringing a fresh and emotive voice to the genre. Her powerful vocals and expressive performances have earned her critical acclaim and a global fanbase.

items.name: Katia Guerreiro
items.description: Katia Guerreiro is a renowned Portuguese fado singer celebrated for her authentic and traditional approach to fado music. She is known for her deep, emotive voice and her dedication to preserving the classic fado style, often performing songs that reflect the cultural and emotional depth of Portuguese heritage.

items.name: Maria Teresa de Noronha
items.description: Maria Teresa de Noronha was a renowned Portuguese fado singer celebrated for her elegant and traditional interpretation of fado music, a genre deeply rooted in Portuguese culture and characterized by its melancholic and expressive nature.

items.name: Carlos do Carmo
items.description: Carlos do Carmo was a celebrated Portuguese fado singer, recognized for his distinctive deep voice and significant contributions to the genre of fado. He helped popularize fado music internationally and was known for blending traditional fado with contemporary influences.

items.name: Dulce Pontes
items.description: Dulce Pontes is a renowned Portuguese singer and songwriter celebrated for her powerful and emotive voice. She is credited with revitalizing the traditional Portuguese music genre of fado by blending it with contemporary and classical influences. Her music often incorporates elements of Portuguese folk, classical, and world music, making her a prominent figure in both national and international music scenes.

items.name: Ana Moura
items.description: Ana Moura is a renowned Portuguese fado singer who has gained international acclaim for her emotive voice and innovative approach to traditional fado music. She blends classic fado elements with contemporary influences, bringing a fresh perspective to the genre while maintaining its deep emotional roots. Moura has released several successful albums and collaborated with various artists, helping to popularize fado worldwide.

items.name: Cristina Branco
items.description: Cristina Branco is a renowned Portuguese fado singer celebrated for her emotive vocal delivery and innovative approach to traditional fado music. She blends classic fado elements with contemporary influences, bringing a fresh perspective to the genre while maintaining its deep emotional roots. Branco has released numerous albums and is recognized for her poetic lyricism and sophisticated musical arrangements.

items.name: Hamid Baroudi
items.description: Hamid Baroudi is a Moroccan singer renowned for his contributions to traditional Arabic and Moroccan folk music. His work often features classic Arabic melodies and rhythms, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of Morocco and the broader Arab world.

items.name: Cheb Bilal
items.description: Cheb Bilal is an Algerian Raï singer renowned for his emotive vocal style and contributions to the Raï music genre, which blends traditional Algerian folk music with contemporary influences. He has gained popularity in North Africa and among Raï music fans worldwide.

items.name: Abdel Ali Slimani
items.description: Abdel Ali Slimani is an Algerian singer recognized for his work in the Raï music genre, which blends traditional Algerian folk music with contemporary influences.

items.name: Lili Boniche
items.description: Lili Boniche was an Algerian Jewish singer renowned for his unique blend of Andalusian, Arabic, and Chaabi music. He was a prominent figure in North African music, celebrated for his smooth vocal style and ability to fuse traditional and popular musical elements.

items.name: Biyouna
items.description: Biyouna is an Algerian singer, actress, and performer renowned for her contributions to Raï and Algerian pop music. She is also known for her work in theater and film, blending traditional Algerian sounds with contemporary influences to create a unique musical and artistic identity.

items.name: Cheb Tarik
items.description: Cheb Tarik is an Algerian raï singer who gained popularity for his fusion of traditional raï music with modern influences, contributing to the global spread of Algerian raï.

items.name: Rachid Taha
items.description: Rachid Taha was an Algerian singer and activist renowned for his innovative fusion of traditional Algerian raï music with rock, electronic, and punk influences. He gained international recognition for his energetic performances and politically charged lyrics that often addressed issues of identity, immigration, and social justice. Taha's music bridged cultural divides and brought North African sounds to a global audience.
